# Hydra

> Hydra keeps a public, tamper-evident record of every build of a dApp frontend. Each push to
> main uploads the build to Swarm and records it on Arkiv (Rabdi testnet, chain 7794095), so
> anyone can check that the site they load matches a published release. Teams add it with one
> API key and one GitHub Actions workflow. Testnet only: no mainnet funds, no gas for the team.

Site: https://hydra-site-one.vercel.app
API: https://hydra-api-5xmn.onrender.com (free tier; the first request after idle can take 30 to 60 s)
Agent skill: https://hydra-site-one.vercel.app/skill/hydra-publish/SKILL.md

## Add Hydra to a repo (what an agent should do)

1. A human gets the API key: open the site, connect a wallet, pick an app name (2 to 40
   lowercase letters, digits, dashes), sign one message (no transaction, no gas). The site then
   shows one block to paste into the agent with the app name, the key and these steps. Without
   that block, an agent stops here and tells the human: "Open the Hydra site, sign in with your
   wallet and paste the block it gives you."
2. The human stores it as a repo secret: `gh secret set HYDRA_API_KEY` (paste when prompted), or
   Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions, New repository secret.
3. The agent adds `.github/workflows/hydra.yml` (template below), with the repo's real install
   and build commands and its build output folder (Vite `dist`, CRA `build`, Next static export
   `out`, Astro `dist`, SvelteKit static `build`).
4. Add the secret before the first push (or re-run the workflow after adding it). Push to main.
   The run prints the Arkiv transaction link. Check with
   `GET https://hydra-api-5xmn.onrender.com/v1/apps/<app>/releases`.

## Workflow template

```yaml
name: hydra

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - run: npm ci && npm run build # replace with the repo's install and build
      - name: Publish to Hydra
        env:
          HYDRA_API_URL: https://hydra-api-5xmn.onrender.com
          HYDRA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HYDRA_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "$HYDRA_API_URL/publish.mjs" -o hydra-publish.mjs
          node hydra-publish.mjs dist # replace dist with the build output folder
```

## Publish script

`publish.mjs` (served by the API) has no dependencies. It reads every file in the build folder,
hashes the external `https` scripts the HTML loads, and POSTs the release. Optional env:
`HYDRA_VERSION` (default `<date>.<Actions run number>`, or `<date>.local` outside CI). Limits: the build must contain `/index.html`, at
most 2000 files and 20 MB. Rate limit: 30 publishes per hour per address.

## API

- `GET /health`: `arkivWrites: true` means publishing works. `swarm: false` means builds are
  recorded on Arkiv but not yet stored on Swarm, so releases show `swarm_ref: pending` (expected
  on this testnet demo until a postage batch is attached).
- `GET /v1/auth/message?address=&app=`: the exact message the wallet signs.
- `POST /v1/auth/key` `{ address, app, issuedAt, signature }`: returns `{ apiKey }`, valid 30 days.
- `POST /v1/releases` with `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`: used by `publish.mjs`.
- `GET /v1/apps/<app>/releases`: releases on Arkiv, newest first.
- `GET /v1/files/sha256-<hex>`: which app and release a file hash belongs to (keep the
  `sha256-` prefix; bare hex returns not found).

## Errors and what to do

- 401: key missing, wrong or expired. Get a new key on the site and update the secret.
- 403 "owned by": getting a key reserves the app name for that wallet on Arkiv, so the site
  refuses a key for that name to any other wallet. Get a new key on the site with another name.
  The reservation is a 30-day lease; every publish renews it to about 6 months, and a name with no
  publish in that time frees itself.
- 429: publish limit for this address. Wait for the hour to pass.
- 400: the message names the problem (no `/index.html`, bad path, too many files).
- 502 with `phase: submitted` or `submission_unknown`: a transaction may exist. Do not re-run
  the publish; check the releases route first. `phase: preflight` is safe to re-run later.

## Rules

- Never put the API key in code, logs, chat or a URL. It lives only in the repo secret.
- Testnets only. Hydra pays the gas; nobody needs funds.
